SFST visits Northern Metropolis
body:
Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui led a delegation of local financial sector representatives to the Northern Metropolis today to review its construction progress. The delegation comprised senior management from the asset management, private equity, insurance, accounting and fintech sectors, alongside representatives from financial regulatory bodies.

 

The group visited the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation & Technology Park, the Kwu Tung North New Development Area (NDA), and the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen NDA. This itinerary allowed them to examine local industrial layouts and assess future investment and financing opportunities. 

 

Through these on-site inspections, delegates gained a comprehensive understanding of the development advantages of "one river, two banks" and "one zone, two parks" in the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone and its synergy with the San Tin Technopole. They also observed the emerging infrastructure in the Kwu Tung North NDA and reviewed Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen’s proximity to Qianhai as a professional services and logistics hub.
 

Discussions also focused on how financial services can support technological innovation and meet the substantial project financing needs driven by Kwu Tung Station, the Northern Link, and local housing plans. The delegation also explored potential the commercial potential of the Hung Shui Kiu Industrial Park, large-scale district developments, and the upcoming University Town.

 

Mr Hui noted that the Chief Executive explicitly highlighted finance as Hong Kong's fundamental strength in the recently announced First Five-Year Plan. He described the Northern Metropolis as the ideal setting to realise the “dual integration” of a “Finance+” strategy with the real economy, positioning the financial sector as an active engine driving strategic transformation.

 

“We organised this visit precisely to enable the financial industry to have the first-hand insights into the land, with a view to comprehensively promoting the integrated development of the financial sector and the real economy,” Mr Hui stated. He added that leveraging market forces and social capital to secure sustainable financial support for local infrastructure, commercial projects, and industry parks remains a key strategy for the Government.

 

“This is also the most vivid embodiment of our full-fledged efforts to drive Hong Kong's evolution from a 'financial city' into a 'finance-empowered city', using finance as a catalyst to boost development in technology, green transition and livelihoods,” he noted.  

 

To support this vision, the Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority are exploring options within the regulatory capital framework for banks to facilitate financing for government-related entities, such as park companies and funded universities. This measure aims to unlock greater financing flexibility to accelerate projects in the area.

 

Furthermore, following updates to the risk-based capital regime for the insurance industry, preferential capital treatment will be introduced for infrastructure investments from December 31 this year. The Government anticipates that this new measure will drive substantial insurance capital into infrastructure projects across the Northern Metropolis development.

title: 5-year plan is HK’s roadmap: CE
body:
Today marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China. It carries the special significance of being the first National Day celebrated since the announcement of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan.

 

Over the past 77 years, the Chinese nation has achieved a historic transformation – from standing up and growing prosperous to becoming strong. Today, China has become the world’s largest manufacturer and merchandise trader, its leading contributor to scientific research output and much more, exerting significant influence on international affairs.

 

The formulation of a Five-Year Plan for Hong Kong is not merely about rolling out a series of policy initiatives. The plan provides a strategic roadmap for Hong Kong, allowing us to apply our unique advantages under “one country, two systems”, embrace modern trends and seize the opportunities brought by national development.

 

Why should we formulate a Five-Year Plan? And why do it now? The answer is straightforward: to fully and swiftly seize the immense opportunities brought by national development, and to deliver more fruits of development to the benefit of our citizens. Faced with an ever-changing geopolitical landscape, the reshaping of industrial chains, as well as the rapid development of technology and artificial intelligence, Hong Kong must devise a strategic roadmap in a proactive manner and put in place forward-looking plans. As the world’s second-largest economy, China is widely recognised as both a driver and a stabiliser for global economic development. Time and tide wait for no man. We must act decisively and respond to changing circumstances by formulating the Five-Year Plan, in order to ride the wave of opportunities, keep pace with the times, and integrate into and serve the overall national development. This can only boost Hong Kong’s progress and allow the people of Hong Kong to enjoy more development dividends.

 

Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is a logical and target-oriented plan. It is based on an overall review of Hong Kong’s prevailing strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats, and it serves as a comprehensive blueprint targeted at building strengths, overcoming weaknesses, seizing opportunities and managing threats. The plan focuses on six themes: first, to strengthen the development of “four centres and one hub”, namely our status as international financial, maritime and trade centres and an international aviation hub, as well as our development into an international innovation and technology centre and an international hub for high-calibre talent; second, to leverage our advantage as an international city by deepening Hong Kong’s development of a legal and dispute resolution services centre, intellectual property trading centre and East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange; third, to expedite the development of the Northern Metropolis; fourth, to reinforce our strength in connecting with the country and the world; fifth, to enhance social well-being; and sixth, to adopt a holistic approach to development and security. These six themes cover economic development, spatial layout, internal and external connectivity, livelihood enhancement, and risk prevention and control, forming a comprehensive system with interconnected and mutually reinforcing components.

 

The three key distinctive features of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan are: first, it is well-suited to the unique characteristics of Hong Kong. In the foreword on page 1 of the plan, it is made clear from the outset that Hong Kong’s Five-Year Plan has to be grounded in the city’s practical reality, and supported by policy measures and major projects that feature Hong Kong's unique character.

 

Second, it adheres to the “one country, two systems” principle. This means that the First Five-Year Plan must be developed under the Basic Law framework. The Basic Law expressly provides for the practice of capitalism and the common law system, as well as the free flow of capital, people, goods and information in Hong Kong, while the First Five-Year Plan stresses a market economy and upholds the two-pronged approach of effective market and capable government.

 

Third, the First Five-Year Plan clearly defines Hong Kong’s international positioning. Its 'International Financial Centre' chapter points out that we must firmly demonstrate Hong Kong’s international positioning, whereas the Policy Address states that we will stay committed to our global positioning. The two documents reiterate the importance and establishment of Hong Kong’s global positioning, which powerfully illustrates that it is part of our city’s DNA.

 

One of the initiatives for implementing the First Five-Year Plan is to fully leverage Hong Kong’s unique advantage as a connector between the country and the rest of the world. Hong Kong is the only city in the world that enjoys the convergence of national and international opportunities. The ultimate focus of the plan is, in fact, to capitalise on this aggregate advantage: drawing on the momentum of the country’s development to gain stable support, while leveraging an international platform to access global resources and achieve two-way interaction. Committed to firmly maintaining its strategic position as the nexus of domestic-international dual circulation, Hong Kong will make greater contributions in its roles as a super connector and super value-adder.

 

As the Chinese saying goes, “Victory is ensured when people pool their strength; success is secured when people put their heads together.” Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is the fruit of the collective wisdom gained during our extensive consultation. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government puts words into action. With a strategic vision for a bright new era that drives reform, boosts development, unleashes opportunities and enhances livelihood, we have formulated the 2026 Policy Address to launch wide-ranging policy measures and take forward the initiatives for the first year in line with our five-year strategic blueprint. I am confident that as long as we, each dedicated to our respective roles, join hands and work in synergy with one another, Hong Kong will certainly be able to set out on a path to a brighter and more prosperous future.

 

Finally, I wish our motherland and Hong Kong continuing prosperity and stability. May all of you enjoy good health and great success in every endeavour. Thank you very much.

 

This is a translation of Chief Executive John Lee’s speech delivered at the reception in celebration of the 77th Anniversary of the Founding of the People’s Republic of China on October 1.

title: IP financing sandbox cases approved
body:
The Government announced today that an initial batch of seven pilot cases under the Intellectual Property Financing Sandbox has successfully secured credit approval. These successful pilot cases span the electronics, construction, toy manufacturing and medical device sectors.

 

The approved loan amounts range from $1 million to $39 million, backed by patent and trade mark assets. This milestone demonstrates that Hong Kong can steadily develop intellectual property (IP) financing while unlocking a new funding channel for enterprises.

 

Participating banks demonstrated flexibility regarding loan values and financing terms during the sandbox pilot. The Commerce & Economic Development Bureau, the Monetary Authority and the Intellectual Property Department will continue to evaluate feedback from stakeholders to shape the next phase of the sandbox.

 

Future expansion plans include increasing the number of participating financial institutions and refining intellectual property valuation processes. Concurrently, the Government today launched a two-year Pilot Patent Valuation Support Scheme through the Hong Kong Technology & Innovation Support Centre.

 

The scheme operates on a one-to-one matching grant model for eligible small and medium-sized enterprises. Approved businesses will receive a one-off funding cap of $80,000 to commission qualified valuation service providers.

 

Opening for applications from today, the initiative aims to leverage professional services to promote IP valuations and provide concrete reference data for credit financing, thereby stimulating a robust local IP trading ecosystem.

 

Originally introduced in last year’s Policy Address, the sandbox serves as an important initiative to promote IP financing. It provides a risk-controlled, collaborative environment for key stakeholders – including financial institutions, enterprises and professional services organisations – to test the full lifecycle of funding arrangements.

 

Adopting a "pioneer and pilot" approach, this initiative allows participants to collectively experiment with asset-backed arrangements, enabling the sector to accumulate vital practical experience.

title: Govt issues 4th digital green bonds
body:
The Government today announced the successful pricing of around HK$20 billion worth of digital green bonds denominated in HK dollars (HKD), Renminbi, US dollars and euros under its Sustainable Bond Programme. 

 

The issuance has once again set a new record for the largest digital bond issuance in the world.

 

It also reinforced the Government's commitment to promoting innovation in the bond market.

 

Alongside traditional settlement rails and the tokenised central bank money option introduced in the previous issuance, tokenised deposits, empowered by EnsembleTX, were incorporated into the primary issuance settlement process for the HKD tranche of this issuance.

 

It represented the world's first digital bond that integrates tokenised deposits in HKD, advancing towards a more integrated digital ecosystem, and laying a foundation for exploring the programmable features of digital money.

 

This issuance also continued to advance adoption of global standards. By adopting the International Capital Market Association's latest Bond Data Taxonomy Version 2.0, the issuance promoted greater data consistency, interoperability and end-to-end automation across the bond lifecycle.

 

Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the Government has successfully issued digital green bonds for the fourth time, totalling HK$20 billion, which is the largest issuance of its kind globally.

 

He highlighted that the offering was oversubscribed, demonstrating strong market appetite for tokenised products issued in Hong Kong.

 

Mr Chan also noted that these bonds, denominated in multiple currencies, cater to the asset diversification needs of both local and overseas investors, and have incorporated a range of innovative technologies to further advance innovation in the bond market.

 

“The Government will continue to issue tokenised bonds on a regular basis, expand the use cases for the underlying technologies, and harness fintech to empower the bond market's continued development," he added.

 

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui said this issuance demonstrated the Government's ongoing commitment to supporting innovative forms of bond issuance and driving green transformation.

 

He added that it will also further enhance society's understanding of the integration of sustainable development and fintech, while strengthening Hong Kong's position as a leading global green and sustainable finance hub.

title: HK’s innovation index ranking rises
body:
Hong Kong's ranking rose by one place to 14th globally among 139 economies and remained 5th in Asia in the Global Innovation Index 2026 published by the World Intellectual Property Organization today.

 

As regards the two sub-indices under the index, Hong Kong's ranking in the "Innovation Input" sub-index remained at 8th globally, while its ranking in the "Innovation Output" sub-index rose by one place to 21st.

 

The Government said that it is pleased to see the good progress Hong Kong has achieved in the index, highlighting that expediting the development of innovation and technology (I&T) has been a policy priority.

 

The Government also noted that it is fully committed to developing Hong Kong into an international I&T centre, following the directions set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

 

Hong Kong will enhance the institutional framework for I&T development, expedite alignment with key national strategies in technology, and develop the new "three major I&T parks and five key research and development institutions" paradigm.

 

The city will also advance new industrialisation accordingly to establish a framework with Hong Kong characteristics for a new industrialisation system, as well as take forward the AI+ Initiative on all fronts by enhancing the layout of computing infrastructure, supporting small and medium-sized enterprises in accelerating their adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), and empowering different sectors of the economy through AI technology.

 

Meanwhile, Hong Kong will leverage the advantage of being closely connected to the Mainland and the world to develop an international hub for science and technology co-operation, as well as deepen the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, thereby attracting global I&T resources and talent.

 

The Government emphasised that it will strive to realise the vision in the Five-Year Plan that Hong Kong will essentially establish an international I&T centre based in the bay area, serving the entire country, while connecting to the world, after 2030.
